assertions.text: Table uses value-set syntax (curly braces like {READ, WRITE} or {READ, WRITE, DELETE}) to express rules that hold across multiple actions
assertions.evidence: Admin can perform any | ADMIN | {READ, WRITE, DELETE} | true

assertions.text: Table has fewer than 9 data rows
assertions.evidence: The table contains 7 data rows (Admin row, 3 User rows, 3 Guest rows)

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
No two rows share both the same Role value and the same boolean output
assertions.evidence: User can read | USER | READ | true and User can write | USER | WRITE | true both have Role=USER and output=true. Similarly, Guest cannot write | GUEST | WRITE | false and Guest cannot delete | GUEST | DELETE | false both have Role=GUEST and output=false. These should be consolidated into {READ, WRITE} and {WRITE, DELETE} value sets respectively.

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title
assertions.evidence: Method name is permissionsByRoleAndAction, which converts to 'Permissions By Role And Action'

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation is present; the assertion accepts this as the table is self-explanatory

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest annotation is present; no ordering violations
